findings.title: Missing viewport-fit=cover defeats every env(safe-area-inset-*) rule on iOS
findings.description: The viewport meta is `content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0"` with no `viewport-fit=cover`. Yet the CSS relies on env(safe-area-inset-*) in four files: topbar.css:4 (.hotbar height calc(3px + env(safe-area-inset-top))), responsive.css:10/53/87/95/144/148 (topbar top padding, actions-menu bottom offset, search panel, note pane, standalone padding), plus note-content.css and noteEnhancements.css.
findings.why: WebKit only resolves env(safe-area-inset-*) to non-zero values when the page opts into the full display area via viewport-fit=cover. Without it, all four insets evaluate to 0 on notched/Dynamic-Island iPhones. Every safe-area guard silently collapses: the mobile '···' actions menu, which is pinned with `bottom: calc(0.6rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))` (responsive.css:53), sits under the home indicator; the standalone PWA topbar padding (responsive.css:144) collapses so the header underlaps the status bar / Dynamic Island; the .hotbar accent renders as a bare 3px strip beneath the notch. This is worst in the installed PWA because apple-mobile-web-app-capable=yes (index.html:7) makes it fullscreen. Chrome/Firefox/desktop are unaffected.
findings.fixSketch: Change the meta to content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0, viewport-fit=cover" so the existing safe-area CSS actually takes effect.

findings.title: theme-color meta is a static light color and is never updated for dark mode
findings.description: Only one `<meta name="theme-color" content="#f4f1e8" />` exists (a light cream). There is no `media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"` variant, and useTheme.ts (cycleTheme / the theme useEffect at useTheme.ts:14-21) only mutates document.documentElement.dataset.theme and localStorage — it never touches the theme-color meta. A grep for theme-color across the whole frontend returns only this single static tag.
findings.why: iOS Safari 15+, the iOS standalone PWA, and Android Chrome paint the browser chrome / status bar band from theme-color. In dark mode the app --bg is #0c0c0a (base.css:98 auto-dark and base.css:51 explicit dark), but the surrounding chrome stays #f4f1e8, producing a bright cream bar clashing with the dark UI. It never corrects when the user cycles to Dark or when the system is dark under theme=auto. Desktop browsers ignore theme-color so they are unaffected. (No apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style is set either, compounding the standalone case.)
findings.fixSketch: Add a second theme-color meta with media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" for the theme=auto path, and in useTheme's effect update the meta's content to match the resolved bg for manual light/dark overrides.

findings.title: Unguarded :hover on a mobile-only element leaves a sticky highlight on touch
findings.description: `.topbar-mobile-path:hover { background: var(--paper-2) }` is not wrapped in @media (hover: hover), unlike the sibling .icon-button and .topbar-search-trigger hovers in the same file (topbar.css:116 and topbar.css:160). This element is rendered ONLY on mobile: topbar.css:242 sets .topbar-mobile-meta { display: none } and responsive.css:44 flips it to display: block below 920px. The same unguarded pattern exists for the explorer/search touch targets (layout-explorer.css:78 .note-link:hover, :164 folder summary:hover; search.css:111/132/159; ui-common.css:23).
findings.why: On touch WebKit/Blink, tapping an element applies :hover and keeps it until the user taps elsewhere (there is no pointer to move away). The mobile path button opens the search overlay rather than navigating, so on return the --paper-2 background stays stuck. The author clearly intended hover to be pointer-gated (they did it for the icon buttons) but missed the touch-only element and the shared explorer/search styles. Purely cosmetic, no data impact.
findings.fixSketch: Wrap these :hover rules in @media (hover: hover) (or :hover:where(...)) so they never fire on touch, matching the existing guarded rules in topbar.css.
